title: A Stroviols, four-string, with two aluminium horns and two bows in fitted case.

A French Violin, circa 1820, L.O.B. 14 3/8in. (365mm), in case. The one-piece back of narrow curl, ribs of similar faint curl, scroll plain, table of open medium grain, varnish of a golden orange yellow brown colour.

A good Violin of the Schmidt in Markneukirchen School, circa 1900, L.O.B. 14 1/4in. (362mm), in case. The attractive one-piece back of medium curl ascending to the right, ribs and scroll of similar curl, table of medium grain, varnish of a golden yellow brown colour. Good condition.

A Violin by Francois Pillement in Mirecourt branded on inner back F. Pillement Pere à Paris, circa 1810, L.O.B. 14 1/4in. (362mm), in case. The one-piece back of narrow curl, ribs and scroll of similar figure, table of narrow grain, varnish of a brown colour on a golden brown ground. Restoration on table otherwise sound.

A Violin by Ernest Mumby bearing the maker's label in London 1930, L.O.B. 14in. (356mm), with a bow in case. The two-piece back and ribs of narrow curl, scroll plain table of narrow grain, varnish of a red colour on a brown ground. Good condition.

A Mittenwald Violin, circa 1880 of the Neuner School labelled Andreas Guarnerius, L.O.B. 14 3/16in. (360mm), with a bow in case. The one-piece back of narrow curl, the ribs of faint curl, the scroll plain, the table of narrow grain, the varnish of a chestnut red brown colour.

A Violin by CH. J. B. COLLIN-MEZIN bearing the maker's label LUTHIER PARIS dated 1923 and signed on the inner lower back, L.O.B. 14in. (355mm), in case. The one-piece back of broad curl, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of broad grain narrowing on the flanks, the varnish of a red brown colour. Post repair on table.

A good Viola by Miles Doubleday bearing the maker's label in London dated 1984, L.O.B. 16 1/8in. (410mm), with a part silver mounted bow by Roderich Paesold stamped on the shaft, in case. The two-piece back and ribs of narrow curl, scroll of similar figure, table of medium grain, varnish of an orange brown colour on a golden brown ground. Mint condition.

A good Markneukirchen Violin, circa 1880 of the ERNST GLASel School, L.O.B. 14 1/8in. (359mm). The two-piece back of medium flame descending from the joint, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of narrow grain widening to the flanks, the transparent varnish of a golden orange colour.

A Munich School Violin, circa 1880 bearing the label Andrea Fiorini fecit, L.O.B. 14 1/8in. (359mm). The handsome one-piece back of mottled curl, the ribs of similar curl, the scroll of narrow curl, the table of narrow grain, the varnish of a clear red brown colour on a yellow ground.

A good French Violin, circa 1820, bearing a label V.ve Parizot, Rue du Pont de la Mousque no. 2, Pres la Bourse à Bourdeaux, L.O.B. 14 5/16in. (363mm). The one-piece back, ribs and scroll of narrow curl, table of narrow grain, widening to medium, varnish of an orange brown colour on a yellow ground. Good condition.

A quarter-size French Violin, circa 1900, L.O.B. 10 7/16in. (265mm). The one-piece back of faint medium curl, ribs and scroll plain, table of medium grain, varnish of an orange red colour on a light brown ground. Minus tailpiece and top nut.

A good Klingenthal School Violin, circa 1790, L.O.B. 14 1/16in. (357mm), with a bow in case. The one-piece back of narrow curl, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of narrow grain, the varnish of a transparent golden brown colour.

A Violin by EMANUEL WHITMARSH bearing the maker's manuscript label in London dated 1900 and inscribed and dated on the lower inner back, L.O.B. 13 15/16in. (354mm). The two-piece back of medium flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of narrow grain, the oil varnish of a clear orange red colour on a yellow ground. Mint condition (a fine example of this maker's work).

A good Mirecourt Violin, circa 1910, labeled Louis Joly à Mirecourt, L.O.B. 14 1/8in. (359mm), with a silver mounted Violin Bow stamped H. E. Blondelet à Paris. The two-piece back of narrow curl descending from the joint, ribs, neck and scroll of similar curl, table of close grain, widening on the flanks, varnish of a red brown colour on a light brown ground. Minor fragment missing right soundhole wing otherwise good condition.

A good German Violin of the Augsburg School, circa 1800, L.O.B. 14in. (355mm). The two-piece back of narrow flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of medium grain, the varnish of a red brown colour on a yellow ground. Minus tailpiece, a peg and fingerboard nut.

A Violin by William Tarr bearing the maker's label in Manchester dated 1881, L.O.B. 14in. (356mm). The one-piece back of narrow flame ascending to the right, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of open broad grain, the transparent varnish of a golden orange colour.

A Mirecourt Violin, circa 1880 of the Laberte School, L.O.B. 14 1/8in. (359mm). The two-piece back of narrow flame, the ribs of similar curl, the scroll almost plain, the table of narrow grain, the varnish of a light orange colour on a yellow ground.

A Violin by Walter H. Mayson bearing the maker's manuscript label in Manchester fecit 1895 and named La Tosca, L.O.B. 14 3/16in. (360mm), in case. The two-piece back of narrow figure with convoluted grain lines showing on the centre outer and inner back, the ribs and scroll of narrow curl, the table of medium grain, the varnish of a red colour on a light brown ground.  With the guarantee and history of the Violin by Stansfield Mayson in Manchester, dated May 1908.

A Violin by CH. J. B. COLLIN-MEZIN bearing the maker's label LUTHIER GRAND PRIX Paris Exposition Universelle and signed on the inner lower back, circa 1920–1930, L.O.B. 13 15/16in. (354mm), with two bows in case. The one-piece back of horizontal narrow curl, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of even medium grain, the varnish of an orange red colour on a yellow ground. Good condition.  With the receipt of CH. J. B. COLLIN-MEZIN.

A Violin by William Atkinson bearing the maker's manuscript label in Tottenham dated 1887, branded below button and fingerboard, L.O.B. 14 1/16in. (357mm), in case. The attractive two-piece back and ribs of narrow curl scroll of broader figure, table of narrow grain, varnish of a red colour on a brown ground.

A French Violin by Hawkes & Son, London, bearing their label dated 1896. The Professor Violin, L.O.B. 14 1/8in. (359mm), with a nickel mounted bow stamped N. LAMBERT. The two-piece back of medium flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of medium grain, the varnish of a transparent orange brown colour. (2)

A Violin, probably Scottish circa 1850, L.O.B. 14 1/16in. (357mm). The two-piece back of narrow flame, the ribs of narrow curl, the scroll plain, the table of medium grain widening on the flanks, the varnish of a clear brown colour. Original neck.

A Violin attributed to Markus Straub in Friedenweiler, circa 1750, bearing a manuscript label, L.O.B. 14 1/16in. (357mm), with bow in case. The two-piece back of narrow flame, ribs of similar curl, scroll plain, table of narrow grain, varnish of a brown colour. Original neck, suitable baroque.

A German Viola, circa 1930, L.O.B. 16 7/16in. (418mm), with a bow in case. The one-piece back of narrow curl ascending to the right, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of medium grain, the varnish of a clear brown colour on a yellow ground.

A Mittenwald Violin, circa 1840 labelled Thomas Earle Hesketh, Manchester fecit 1900, L.O.B. 14 3/8in. (365mm), with a bow in case. The two-piece back of narrow flame, the ribs and scroll of similar figure, the table of medium grain, the varnish of a clear orange brown colour.

A good French Violin, circa 1900 labelled Craigs Celebrated Violins and dated 1899, L.O.B. 14 1/8in. (359mm), with a bow in case. The two-piece back of medium flame descending from the joint, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of narrow grain widening to the flanks, the varnish of a light orange colour.

A French Violin, circa 1920 labelled LEON PAROCHE, Billancourt, L.O.B. 14 1/8in. (359mm), with a bow in case. The one-piece back of narrow curl, the ribs of similar figure, the scroll plain, the table of medium grain, the varnish of an orange red brown colour. Minus endpin and tailpiece.

A good Mittenwald Violin of the Neuner School, circa 1880, L.O.B. 14 1/4in. (362mm), with a bow in case. The two-piece back of narrow flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of broad grain, the varnish of a red brown colour. Minus pegs, endpin.

A Neapolitan Violin, circa 1860, L.O.B. 13 7/8in. (352mm), with a bow in a shaped walnut wood case. The two-piece back of narrow curl ascending slightly from the joint, the ribs of similar faint figure, the scroll plain, the table of broad open slightly wavy grain, the varnish of a clear transparent brown colour. Good condition.

A Violin by G. CERPI bearing the maker's label in Mirecourt dated 1904, L.O.B. 14 1/8in. (359mm), with two bows (one half-size) in case. The two-piece back of medium flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of narrow grain, the varnish of a clear red colour on a yellow ground.
A silver mounted French Violin Bow branded CARRODUSS on the shaft, the ebony frog with pearl eyes, the round stick of a brown colour, 55gms.

A French Violin bearing the label Paul Bailly Luthier 1884 and branded BAILLY below the button, L.O.B. 14 1/8in. (359mm), in shaped case. The two-piece back of faint narrow figure, the ribs and scroll plain, the table of strong narrow grain, the varnish of a brown colour on a light brown ground.

A Violin, probably Flemish, circa 1830, L.O.B. 14 3/16in. (360mm), with a bow in a walnut veneer case. The two-piece back of narrow curl broadening in the upper back, the ribs of narrow curl, the scroll of similar curl, the table of even narrow grain, the varnish of a golden brown colour, the scroll red on a yellow ground. Table fair.

A Violin, circa 1900, L.O.B. 14 1/16in. (357mm), with a bow in case. The one-piece back of faint broad curl, the ribs of similar curl, the scroll plain, the table of narrow grain, the varnish of a red brown colour on a yellow ground.

An interesting Violin bearing a manuscript label dated 1918, L.O.B. 14 1/16in. (357mm), in case. The one-piece back elaborately carved with foliate designs, the centre depicting a medieval castle in relief, the ribs of medium curl, the pegbox and volute similarly carved with leaf design, the table of medium grain, the soundholes of rugged outline, the varnish of a brown colour on a yellow ground.

A Violin by Wolff Bros., bearing the maker's label in Kreuznach dated 1887, L.O.B. 14 1/8in. (357mm), with a bow in case. The two-piece back of medium flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of medium grain, the varnish of a red colour on a brown ground.

A Violin by Edwin Pollard in Blackpool, bearing the maker's label dated 1914, L.O.B. 14 1/8in. (359mm), with a bow in case and cover. The two-piece back and ribs of narrow figure, the scroll almost plain, the table of broad grain, the varnish of a clear yellow amber colour.

A Viola by Ernest Mumby bearing the maker's manuscript label in London dated 1940, L.O.B. 16in. (405mm), with a silver mounted bow by Aug. Edwin Prager, stamped on the shaft, as seen, in shaped lined viola case. The attractive one-piece back of convoluted grain, cut on the slab, ribs and scroll of medium curl, table of medium grain varnish of a red brown colour on a light brown ground. Good condition.

A Violin by Ernest Mumby bearing the maker's undated manuscript label in London, L.O.B. 14 1/16in. (357mm), with two bows in case. The one-piece back of mottled curl, ribs of similar figure, scroll plain, table of medium grain, varnish of a red brown colour on a light brown ground. Good condition.

A Violin by Albyn Ludwig Paulus branded on top block, in Markneukirchen bearing the label Gustav Schwarz Violinmacher Wien, circa 1900, L.O.B. 14 5/16in. (363mm), in case. The attractive one-piece back of medium curl, ribs and scroll of narrow curl, table of medium grain, varnish of a golden yellow colour. Minor repair on table otherwise good condition.

A Violin of the Heberlein School in Markneukirchen, circa 1870, L.O.B. 14 5/16in. (363mm), in case. The two-piece back of narrow curl, ribs and scroll of similar curl, table of medium grain, varnish of a red brown colour on a golden brown ground. Minor repairs.

A good French Violin, circa 1910, L.O.B. 13 15/16in. (354mm), with a bow in shaped case. The two-piece back of narrow flame, the ribs and scroll of faint broad curl, the table of narrow grain, the transparent varnish of a golden orange colour. Good condition.

A Mirecourt Violin by Thibouville Lamy, circa 1900, labelled ECOLE GRANDINI, L.O.B. 14 1/8in. (359mm). The two-piece back of narrow flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of medium grain, the varnish of an orange brown colour on a yellow ground. Good condition.

A Violin by OSCAR PRAGER bearing the maker's label in Mittenwald, dated 1924, no. 124, L.O.B. 14 3/16in. (360mm). The two-piece back of medium flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of narrow grain widening on the flanks, the transparent varnish of an orange colour on a yellow ground.

A good Viola by L. A. PERRY bearing the maker's label in DEGANWY, signed and dated 1984, L.O.B. 16 1/4in. (415mm), in shaped case. The one-piece back of narrow curl, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of even medium grain, the clear varnish of a golden orange colour.

A good Viola by William H. Jones bearing the maker's manuscript label in Tipton, anno 1954, no. 9, L.O.B. 16 3/4in. (425mm), in case. The two-piece back of narrow curl, the ribs and scroll of medium curl, the table of medium grain, the clear varnish of a golden orange colour on a yellow ground.

A silver mounted Viola Bow by L. GILLET stamped on the shaft. The ivory frog with pearl eye and ring, the adjuster of silver, the round stick of a deep red brown colour. An almost invisible repair in the stick at the lapping, 78gms.  Gillet worked with E. Sartory.

A Memorial Violin by LOUIS LOWENDALL bearing the maker's signed label fecit Dresden Anno 1884, L.O.B. 14 1/4in. (362mm), in case. The one-piece back, ribs and scroll japanned black with engraved pokerwork designs of foliage, birds and bees, the pine table similarly adorned. Good condition.

A good Mirecourt Violin by Thibouville Lamy, circa 1920 with the VIRTUOSE label, L.O.B. 14 3/16in. (360mm), in case. The two-piece back of narrow flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of broad grain narrowing to the flanks, the varnish of a red-brown colour on a yellow ground.

A French Violin, circa 1920, L.O.B. 14 1/8in. (359mm), in case. The one-piece back of medium curl, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of narrow grain, the varnish of a golden orange colour.

A good Mirecourt Violin, circa 1920, L.O.B. 14 1/8in. (359mm), in case. The two-piece back of narrow flame ascending from the joint, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of medium grain, the varnish of a red brown colour on a yellow ground.

A French Violin, circa 1830 of the Nicolas Aine School, L.O.B. 14 3/16in. (360mm). The one-piece back and ribs of narrow curl, the scroll of similar figure, the table of narrow grain broadening on the flanks, the varnish of an orange brown colour on a golden brown ground. Restoration required.

A Viola, circa 1880 labelled Stefano Scarampella di Brescia anno 1900, L.O.B. 15 3/16in. (385mm). The two-piece back of narrow figure, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of strong medium grain, the varnish of a deep red brown colour on a yellow ground.

A Violin by Francois Barzoni, circa 1900 bearing the maker's torn label Manufacture Speciale de Beare & Sons, Londres, L.O.B. 14 1/8in. (359mm), with a bow in shaped leather case with cover. The two-piece back of medium flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of narrow grain widening to the flanks, the transparent varnish of a red brown colour.

An interesting Violin, circa 1760–1770 labelled JOANNES FLORENUS GUIDANTUS FECIT BONONIAE ANNO 1711, L.O.B. 14in. (355mm). The two-piece back of faint narrow flame (a wing in the make on lower right flank), the ribs of similar curl, the scroll plain), the table of medium grain, the varnish of a red brown colour on a yellow brown ground. (Some marks on the back centre joint showing removed tape).
A Mittenwald Violin, circa 1840, L.O.B. 14in. (356mm), in case. The one-piece back of narrow curl, the ribs and scroll of less figure, the table of broad grain, the varnish of a red brown colour.

A good Mirecourt Violin by J.T.L., circa 1940, L.O.B. 14 3/16in. (360mm). The two-piece back of medium flame, ribs and scroll of similar curl, table of medium grain, the transparent varnish of an orange colour on a yellow ground. Good condition.

An interesting Violin of the Nurnberg School, circa 1780, L.O.B. 14 3/16in. (360mm), with a bow in case. The two-piece back of narrow curl, the ribs of broad curl, the scroll plain, the table of medium grain, the varnish of a red brown colour on a yellow ground. A repair on left flank back.

A good Violin by ALBERT STARK bearing the maker's label LUTHIER STRASBOURG anno 1913, L.O.B. 14 1/8in. (359mm), in case. The two-piece back of broad flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of medium grain, the varnish of a clear red colour.

A Violin by KARL MULLER bearing the label in BUBENREUTH dated 1984 from the workshops of J. P. GUIVIER, L.O.B. 14 1/8in. (357mm), with two bows (one by Albert Fischer), in case with cover. The two-piece back of medium flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of narrow grain, the varnish of a red brown colour. (Note strung with viola strings).

A Neapolitan Violin, circa first half 19th-century bearing the label ANTONIUS GAGLIANO FILIUS NICOLAI FECIT NEAP 1838 and in manuscript Via Ciriglio, L.O.B. 13 7/8in. (352mm). The two-piece back of narrow flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of medium grain widening on the flanks, the clear varnish of a golden brown amber colour.

An interesting Violin, probably Tyrolese, circa 1860 bearing the label CARLO GIUSEPPE TESTORE IN CONTRADA LARGA DI MILANO AL SEGNO DELL AQUILA 1697, L.O.B. 14in. (356mm), in a shaped leather case with cover. The one-piece back cut on the slab showing convoluted grain, the ribs and scroll plain, the table of medium grain widening to the flanks, the varnish of a clear orange brown colour.
A silver mounted Violin Bow by C. THOMASSIN A PARIS stamped on the shaft. The ebony frog with pearl eyes, the adjuster of silver with ebony sandwich, the round stick of a red brown colour, 58gms.

A fine VIOLA by STEFANO CONIA bearing the maker's label Fatto in Cremona Anno 1978, no. 312, with signature, L.O.B. 16 3/4in. (425mm), in case with cover. The one-piece back of mottled curl, the ribs and scroll of medium curl, the table of medium grain, the varnish of a red colour on a yellow ground.  With the certificate of the maker dated Nov. 1978.

A silver mounted tortoiseshell frog Violin Bow by W. E. Hill & Sons, stamped W. E. Hill & Sons on the shaft. The tortoiseshell frog with pearl eye and ring, the adjuster of silver and tortoiseshell, the round stick with silver face of a red brown colour. Fine condition, 60gms.

An interesting Italian Violin, circa 1720 bearing the label JOSEPH GUARNERIUS filius ANDREAE fecit CREMONAE SUB TITULO S. TERESIAE (date erased), L.O.B. 13 7/8in. (352mm), upper bouts 6 7/16in. (163mm), lower bouts 7 15/16in. (202mm), in case. The one-piece back of broad curl, the ribs of faint broad figure, the table of medium grain (wavy on the upper right flank), the scroll plain, in the style of DEL GESU, the varnish of a red brown colour. The back with four repairs, is lined, table half edged.

An Italian Violin bearing the label of GAETANO POLLASTRI fece in BOLOGNA 1931 with the brand on the inner back and bottom rib of two chickens, L.O.B. 14 1/16in. (358mm). The one-piece back of medium curl, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of strong narrow grain widening to medium on the flanks, the varnish of a red brown colour.  With the certificate of GIUSEPPE ORNATI dated MILAN 1962.

A Violin by LAURENTIUS BELLAFONTANA bearing the maker's label FECIT GENUAE ANNO DOMINI 1976 with the maker's brand L. BELLAFONTANA GENOVA on the upper label and top block, L.O.B., 13 15/16in. A fine Violin by William H. Luff bearing the maker's label in London, dated 1978, L.O.B. 13 15/16in. (355mm), in case. A good and handsome Violin by EUGENIO DEGANI bearing the maker's label (DIECI MEDAGLIE DI MERITO) Fece VENEZIA ANNO 1893. L.O.B. 14 3/8in. (365mm) in shaped leather case.
